name: Title
voice: This is Phophy: an iPhone app that understands your photos.

name: Scenario 1: scrolling
screen: Scrolling the whole library; a clock counts the minutes
voice: Last month you photographed a whiteboard. You remember what was on it, but it's buried under hundreds of newer photos. You scroll, and give up.

name: Scenario 1: found
screen: Typing "whiteboard from last month"; photos, the answer, the photo opened
voice: With Phophy, just type what you remember: whiteboard from last month. The matching photos appear at once, and the answer tells you when and where it was taken.

name: Scenario 2: the slides
screen: Seven slide photos dealt out, then swept into a pile
voice: Second scenario. In today's lecture you photographed seven slides. Like most of us, you will never open them again.

name: Scenario 2: ask
screen: Asking "Summarise the slides from today's lecture"
voice: Ask Phophy to summarise the slides from today's lecture. It picks out today's slides and sums them up.

name: Scenario 2: notes
screen: Make notes; summary; key points; a flashcard turned over
voice: Or tap Make notes. On the phone, Phophy writes a summary, lists the key points with their slide numbers, and makes flashcards, so the photos you took actually get reviewed.

name: Ask: receipt
screen: "How much did I spend at Muji?" answered HK$702
voice: It also answers from what's inside a photo. How much did I spend at Muji? It reads the receipt.

name: Edit
screen: Editor: "warmer and more vivid", done on the iPhone
voice: To edit, describe the change. Simple edits run on the phone; bigger ones can go to an AI image service you choose.

name: Collections
voice: Collections sorts the library for you: slides, receipts, documents, people, pets. It also finds near-identical shots and suggests which one to keep.

name: Place and time
screen: "Tokyo in May"; the answer; all results as an album
voice: Search understands places and dates in plain words, like Tokyo in May, and opens every result as an album.

name: Privacy
screen: Settings: Apple Intelligence and cloud AI switches
voice: All of this runs on the phone by default. Cloud AI is only used if you turn it on.

name: Results
screen: Search before and after, four bars
voice: We measured search on the Flickr30k benchmark. Against our first version, Chinese searches rose from 2 to 51 percent, misspelled ones from 13 to 59, and objects found from 51 to 89 percent.

name: iPhone speed
screen: Under 25 ms per search; 1.5 s per description; 0 uploads
voice: On a real iPhone 13 Pro Max, a search takes under 25 milliseconds, and no photo is uploaded.
